newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL'S SANTOS SAYS SOLVED SHORT-STAFFING PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL'S SANTOS SAYS SOLVED SHORT-STAFFING PROBLEM.

text.p: Santos port authority CODESP has smoothed out some problems in implementing 24-hour operations at the port and earlier delays in loading vessels have now been eliminated, a spokeswoman said.

Shipping agency Transcar last week reported not all shifts at Santos port were properly staffed after the port switched to operating 24 hours a day and as a result, some vessels were waiting longer than usual.

"CODESP has already managed to overcome this problem. There is no longer a problem of short-staffing, in fact there is now more personnel available than positions to fill," the port authority spokeswoman said.
CODESP solved the problem by adding extra workers to two categories which were short-staffed, she said.

On Wednesday, one vessel was loading soybeans at the public terminal and two vessels were waiting to dock to load soybeans. Seven vessels were loading bagged sugar, one bulk sugar and one unspecified. Two vessels were waiting to dock to load bulk sugar and three to load sugar (unspecified).
At Paranagua port, waiting times for soybeans and soymeal were little changed from 10 days ago, when traders had expressed concern about slow loading and a possible lack of stocks at the port.
Vessels were waiting 13 to 15 days for soybeans, compared with 15 to 16 days more than a week ago. For soymeal, the waiting time was 14 to 16 days, up from nine to 10 days.
Rain has halted the loading of grains since Monday, but waiting times were fairly normal for this time of year, said a Transcar shipping agent. "Stocks are good," he added.
There were 221,900 tonnes of soybeans in stock, as well as 150,600 tonnes soymeal and roughly 124,000 tonnes soymeal pellets, he said.
